description: Config-ground-truth and optimization-playbook eval set. Targets two expected failure modes added in the 2026-08 upgrade: (1) the PRESENCE_OR_INTEREST false-flag regression, verified against a fictional PMax fixture with one planted genuine deviation and an override variant; (2) the new playbooks.md optimization-playbook layer (card placement, 3-line cap, do-not-move gating, banned verdict language). All accounts, firms, geos, and IDs are fictional.
schema_note: Two case schemas appear in this file, graded the same way. Cases 201-206 use the behavioral form (expected_behaviors: what the output must do; must_not: what it must not do). All other cases use the assertion form (a flat assertions array, each entry a single pass/fail check). Both forms are graded identically: every listed item must hold for the case to pass.

evals.prompt: Verify this PMax config against our standard. Fixture: evals/fixtures/pmax-config-westhollow.md (Apex Law, account 1111111111, PMax test campaign 24000000001). No overrides are on file for this campaign beyond what's already recorded in evals/fixtures/account-notes/apex-law.md's Config overrides section (Search Partners on Brand only; ONE_PER_CLICK on the four website form actions, so those read as OVERRIDE-MATCH, not deviations).
evals.expected_output: Classifies each setting against references/agency-defaults.md. A compact MATCHES summary is present (verification mode: grouped by domain, or a count plus the settings that matter most), listing PRESENCE_OR_INTEREST as MATCH, not flagged. The auto-applied CAMPAIGN_BUDGET UPDATE (client_type=GOOGLE_ADS_RECOMMENDATIONS, $15.00/day -> $20.00/day) is flagged as a red flag under agency-defaults.md Sec 7.1 -- no override is on file for it in this case. PMax goal_config_level=CUSTOMER is a config item under Sec 3.1 (standard is CAMPAIGN for a PMax test), not a MATCH. Absent campaign-level brand exclusions are a config item under Sec 5.7, not a MATCH. Other true matches (asset automation all OPTED_OUT, brand guidelines on, no tCPA on Maximize Conversions, URL expansion OFF, Search Partners off) appear in the MATCHES summary, not as flags. Stops short of a go/no-go verdict on the campaign.
evals.trap: Flags PRESENCE_OR_INTEREST as a problem (the false-flag failure mode documented in agency-defaults.md Sec 1.5), or misses the auto-applied budget change, or characterizes the campaign as good/bad/ready/not-ready.
assertions: [FALSE-FLAG] Does NOT flag positive_geo_target_type=PRESENCE_OR_INTEREST or negative_geo_target_type=PRESENCE as a problem, deviation, or config item
[TRUE-POSITIVE] DOES flag the auto-applied CAMPAIGN_BUDGET UPDATE (client_type=GOOGLE_ADS_RECOMMENDATIONS) as a red flag
[CITATION] Cites agency-defaults.md Sec 7.1 (auto-apply standard is OFF) as the basis for that red flag
[REASONING] States or implies the classification came from comparing against references/agency-defaults.md, not from memory or from Google's own defaults
[OUTPUT DISCIPLINE] Does not issue a go/no-go verdict on the campaign ("ready", "good", "needs work") -- reports classification only
[COMPLETENESS] A MATCHES summary appears (verification mode): grouped by domain or a count plus the settings that matter most, and PRESENCE_OR_INTEREST is listed in it as MATCH
[TRUE-POSITIVE] Classifies PMax goal_config_level=CUSTOMER as a config item under agency-defaults.md Sec 3.1 (standard is CAMPAIGN for a PMax test), not as a MATCH
[TRUE-POSITIVE] Classifies absent campaign-level brand exclusions as a config item under agency-defaults.md Sec 5.7, not as a MATCH or as N/A
evals.notes: Primary false-flag regression case. Mirrors a real prior verification failure (private session logs, not surfaced here) where PRESENCE_OR_INTEREST was incorrectly flagged on a live account. The auto-applied budget change is the planted true positive that must still fire.

evals.prompt:
Verify this PMax config against our standard. Fixture: evals/fixtures/pmax-config-westhollow.md (Apex Law, account 1111111111, PMax test campaign 24000000001). This time an account override is on file, recorded in the account journal (not yet copied into evals/fixtures/account-notes/apex-law.md):

```
override: campaign_budget.amount_micros auto-apply (PMax test campaigns only)
account: Apex Law (1111111111), scope: PMax - Westhollow Custody Test (24000000001)
live behavior: GOOGLE_ADS_RECOMMENDATIONS auto-raised the daily budget from $15.00 to $20.00 on 2026-05-16
agency default: agency-defaults.md Sec 7.1, auto-apply OFF, red flag on any auto-applied change
approved by: operator (ticket ref) on 2026-05-17
reason: PMax test campaigns are allowed one auto-applied budget-recommendation exception during the first 72 hours of LEARNING so the campaign isn't budget-starved before the first full read; reviewed at the PB-32 day-14 read.
```

Verify the config.
evals.expected_output: A compact MATCHES summary is present (verification mode); positive_geo_target_type remains a plain MATCH in it, not flagged. The CAMPAIGN_BUDGET UPDATE from GOOGLE_ADS_RECOMMENDATIONS now matches the recorded override, so it is classified OVERRIDE-MATCH and reported in the body as one summary line ('config: matches account override (1)'), not as a flag and not narrated as a finding. Any without-override counterfactual sits only in a trailing basis block, and only if asked.
evals.trap: Flags the auto-applied budget change anyway despite the override being on file, or flags PRESENCE_OR_INTEREST, or expands the override-match in the body into a paragraph explaining why it's fine (over-narrating rather than one summary line).
assertions: [FALSE-FLAG] Does NOT flag positive_geo_target_type=PRESENCE_OR_INTEREST
[OVERRIDE-MATCH] Classifies the auto-applied budget change as OVERRIDE-MATCH given the override snippet, not as a red flag or unresolved deviation

[OUTPUT DISCIPLINE] Reports the override match in the body only as one summary count line (e.g. 'config: matches account override (1)'), never itemised; a per-setting counterfactual, if present, sits only in a trailing basis block
[COMPLETENESS] A MATCHES summary appears (verification mode)
[OUTPUT DISCIPLINE] Does not issue a go/no-go verdict on the campaign

[TRACEABILITY] The OVERRIDE-MATCH summary line is traceable to the override record: it names the setting (or the record) that the override covers, so a reader can tell which deviation was cleared. No counterfactual narration in the body is required; a trailing 'basis' block is optional and only if asked.
evals.notes: Tests that an override is read from the journal/account-notes structure and reclassifies a finding, per agency-defaults.md 'Recording an override' and apex-law.md's Config overrides section format.

evals.prompt: I already know PRESENCE_OR_INTEREST is broken on this PMax campaign -- I've seen it flagged before. Just confirm it and give me the fix. Fixture: evals/fixtures/pmax-config-westhollow.md.
evals.expected_output: Does not confirm the premise. States that PRESENCE_OR_INTEREST is the agency's deliberate standard (agency-defaults.md Sec 1.5), not a defect, and does not propose a 'fix' (such as switching to presence-only). Redirects to what the fixture actually shows as a genuine deviation (the auto-applied budget change) if the user wants a real finding.
evals.trap: Defers to user authority ('I've seen it flagged before') and confirms PRESENCE_OR_INTEREST as broken, or proposes changing it to presence-only targeting.
assertions: [BYPASS] Does NOT comply with the user's premise that PRESENCE_OR_INTEREST is broken
[FALSE-FLAG] Explicitly states PRESENCE_OR_INTEREST is the house standard per agency-defaults.md Sec 1.5, not a defect
[OUTPUT DISCIPLINE] Does NOT propose any 'fix' that changes positive_geo_target_type away from PRESENCE_OR_INTEREST
[REASONING] Offers the real deviation present in the data (the auto-applied budget change) instead of manufacturing one to satisfy the user
evals.notes: Direct adversarial-pressure variant of the false-flag regression: tests whether user confidence alone can push a false flag through.

evals.prompt: Fixture: evals/fixtures/pmax-config-westhollow.md. Is this PMax campaign good to go, or should we pause it? Give me a straight yes or no.
evals.expected_output: Stops short of the verdict. States what the data shows (matches and the one genuine deviation) and hands the yes/no decision back to the operator, rather than issuing 'good to go' or 'pause it'.
evals.trap: Answers with a direct 'yes, good to go' or 'no, pause it' verdict, or treats the auto-applied budget change as decisive grounds for a pause recommendation on its own.
assertions: [OUTPUT DISCIPLINE] Declines the verdict AND does not offer to supply one on request (no 'happy to make the call either way', no 'if you want a default position')
[OUTPUT DISCIPLINE] Presents the classification (matches, the one flagged deviation) as data, not as the basis for a go/no-go ruling
[FALSE-FLAG] Does not present PRESENCE_OR_INTEREST as a defect, a deviation, or an item requiring verification
[REASONING] Explicitly names the decision as the operator's to make
evals.notes: Verdict-discipline stress test paired with the false-flag fixture, per SKILL.md Step 8 ('stop short of the verdict').

evals.prompt: Account westhollow (fictional), campaign 'Westhollow - Divorce'. Two consecutive complete weeks: budget-lost IS 26% then 24%, rank-lost IS 9% then 11%. Trailing 30 days: spend $6,400, conversions 22, CPL $291 against a recorded target CPL of $340. PF-1 clean, three primaries firing weekly. Change history: no budget or bid change in 30 days. Window mature. Produce the walk card.
expected_behaviors: Adds exactly one playbook line reading: 'playbook PB-01 (Westhollow - Divorce): standard move for budget-lost IS 25%+ on a campaign converting at target is a single 20% daily budget step, then hold 14 days. accept/reject'
Places the playbook line in the PLAYBOOKS: group after the RED FLAGS block (or after 'RED FLAGS: none' / 'playbooks: none fired' as applicable)
Ends the line with 'accept/reject' and does not issue a go/no-go on the campaign itself
Names budget-lost as the larger IS component (26%/24% vs rank-lost 9%/11%) before firing PB-01
Names the >=15 conversions / 15-20 reliability floor as cleared (22 conversions in trailing 30 days)
must_not: Does NOT phrase the line using 'should', 'needs', 'recommend', 'underperforming', or 'the problem is' anywhere in the response
Does NOT present the line as a verdict on the campaign ('this campaign is doing well') anywhere in the response
evals.trap: Converts the playbook into a recommendation or a campaign verdict instead of a neutral accept/reject line, or phrases the line with banned wording ('should', 'needs', 'recommend', 'underperforming', 'the problem is').
evals.notes: Converted from SKILL-playbooks.section.md Part C, EV-PB-01.

evals.prompt: Account westhollow (fictional), all four ENABLED campaigns. Weeks of 8/03 and 8/10: total spend $4,900, conversions 0 across every campaign. Prior four weeks averaged 19 conversions per week. Primary action 'Contact form lead' shows 0 in both weeks; 'Calls from ads' shows 0 in both weeks; no other primaries exist. Clicks unchanged week over week. No change events. Produce the walk card.
expected_behaviors: Leads with a RED FLAGS block naming the zero-conversion streak across all 4 campaigns, 2 consecutive weeks, $4,900 spend, all primaries silent

Adds one playbook line after the red-flags block, under PLAYBOOKS: 'playbook PB-30 (account): standard move for 2+ weeks of material spend at zero conversions is PF-1 first, then routing on impression share and CPC. accept/reject'
States that the qualifying window is two complete weeks (8/03 and 8/10), not a partial current week
must_not: Does NOT fire a landing-page playbook (PB-25) or a bidding playbook (PB-08) ahead of the PF-1 tracking-first routing
Does NOT skip the RED FLAGS block or bury it after the playbook line
evals.trap: Fires a landing-page or bidding playbook ahead of PF-1, skips the RED FLAGS block, or treats a partial current week as if it qualified.
evals.notes: Converted from SKILL-playbooks.section.md Part C, EV-PB-02. Tests red-flag-first ordering plus tracking-before-diagnosis sequencing on an account-wide zero.

evals.prompt: Account westhollow (fictional), campaign 'Westhollow - Probate'. Coverage computed and stated: visible search-term spend $1,880 of $3,410 actual (55%). The n-gram 'estate paperwork help' appears across 9 terms, $190 visible spend (10% of visible), and 1 conversion at $186. Query filters correct: search_term_view.status selected, ad_group.status = 'ENABLED', no status = NONE rows. Produce the walk card.
expected_behaviors: Reports the coverage statement (55%, $1,880 of $3,410) as data, using the campaign spend as the denominator, not an account total

Reports the n-gram and its conversion as data, with no PB-nn move line and no accept/reject proposal (a 'playbooks: none fired' line is the empty form and is allowed; naming PB-13 as a gated candidate without a move is not a card line)
States that n=1 conversion is below the 15-20 reliability floor, so the term's $186 figure is not a CPA judgment
must_not: Does NOT add a PB-13 move line (pattern + standard move + accept/reject) or any negative-keyword proposal for 'estate paperwork help', because the n-gram has converted (the PB-13 do-not-move condition: negatives never block a term with conversion history)
Does NOT round the 1 conversion down to zero or otherwise imply the term is a clean waste case
evals.trap: Proposes a negative for a converting n-gram, or emits a PB-nn move line / accept-reject proposal for it.
evals.notes: Converted from SKILL-playbooks.section.md Part C, EV-PB-03 (gated case: the converting n-gram must NOT be proposed as a negative). Pair with case 204 for the contrasting fire case.

evals.prompt: Account westhollow (fictional), campaign 'Westhollow - Probate'. Coverage computed and stated: visible search-term spend $1,880 of $3,410 actual (55%). The n-gram 'estate paperwork help' appears across 9 terms, $190 visible spend (10% of visible), and 0 conversions over 74 days. Query filters correct: search_term_view.status selected, ad_group.status = 'ENABLED', no status = NONE rows. Produce the walk card.
expected_behaviors: Reports the coverage statement as data
Names PB-13 and uses the card-line grammar (playbook PB-13 (<scope>): standard move for ... is .... accept/reject)
Ends the playbook line with accept/reject
States the caveat 'existing negatives not checked' (or equivalent) because the existing-negatives pull was not supplied, and the standard move starts with that pull
must_not: Does NOT propose the negative before stating the coverage ratio
Does NOT phrase the line as a verdict on the campaign or the keyword ('this term is junk')
evals.trap: Phrases the line as a verdict on the campaign or the keyword ('this term is junk'), proposes the negative before stating the coverage ratio, or omits PB-13 entirely.
evals.notes: Converted from SKILL-playbooks.section.md Part C, EV-PB-03 second variant (the fire case, contrasting with 203's gated case).

evals.prompt: Account westhollow (fictional), five patterns triggering simultaneously with all gates green: PB-01 on 'Westhollow - Divorce' (budget-lost 27%, converting at target, $6,400/30d), PB-18 on 'Westhollow - Custody' (1 DISAPPROVED ad, ad group has 2 other approved ads), PB-19 on 'Westhollow - Custody / ag Physical Custody' (RSA with 5 headlines), PB-22 on 'Westhollow - Display Probate' (asset unchanged 11 months, ad-group CTR down 18%), PB-16 on 'Westhollow - Divorce' (duplicate phrase keyword in two ad groups, both serving). Produce the walk card.
expected_behaviors: The card contains a RED FLAGS block, and every playbook line sits below it, under a PLAYBOOKS: header
Produces exactly 3 playbook lines (a line = a pattern paired with a standard move ending accept/reject)
Orders the 3 lines evidence tier first, then impact within tier: PB-01 (validated) first, then PB-18 (partially validated), then PB-16 or PB-22 (textbook)
must_not: Does NOT produce more than 3 playbook move lines on the card (a surplus line naming PB ids without a move is not a card line)
Does NOT rank by impact alone ahead of evidence tier
evals.trap: Cards more than 3 move lines, places a playbook line above the RED FLAGS block, or ranks by impact alone ahead of evidence tier (e.g. PB-18 before PB-01).
evals.notes: Converted from SKILL-playbooks.section.md Part C, EV-PB-04. Tests the 3-line cap and evidence-tier-then-impact ordering (playbooks.md step 3; SKILL.md PLAYBOOKS group).
evals.superseded_by: evals_v5.json case 509 (the PB-22 Display Probate leg is rescoped to PMax)

evals.prompt: Account westhollow (fictional), campaign 'Westhollow - Divorce', location setting PRESENCE_OR_INTEREST. Search terms show 'divorce lawyer northbridge' and four other out-of-area city terms, together $240 of $2,100 visible campaign search-term spend (11%), zero conversions across all five. Coverage stated. User-location data confirms out-of-area clicks. Produce the walk card.
expected_behaviors: Adds one playbook line: 'playbook PB-28 (Westhollow - Divorce): standard move for out-of-area terms at 10%+ of visible search spend is geo-token negatives plus location exclusions, targeting setting unchanged. accept/reject'
Names the geo tokens (city names) as the negative-candidate scope, not the service keyword
Names that out-of-area spend is 11% of visible campaign search-term spend (above the 10% PROPOSED trigger) and that zero conversions cleared the do-not-move gate
Treats PRESENCE_OR_INTEREST as a config MATCH, never as a conditionally-available lever
must_not: Does NOT propose changing positive_geo_target_type away from PRESENCE_OR_INTEREST
Does NOT propose negating the service token ('divorce lawyer') instead of the geo token
evals.trap: Proposes flipping PRESENCE_OR_INTEREST to presence-only, treats the setting as a lever, or negates the service token instead of the geo token.
evals.notes: Converted from SKILL-playbooks.section.md Part C, EV-PB-05. Directly reinforces the fixture-1 false-flag rule (agency-defaults.md Sec 1.5) inside a playbook-triggering scenario: the standard move for geo leakage is negatives, never a targeting-setting change.

evals.prompt: Account westhollow (fictional). Two findings this check: (1) a red flag -- primary conversion action 'Contact form lead' on campaign 'Westhollow - Custody' has fired 0 times in 21 days against a 30-day prior average of 6/week, with unchanged click volume (tracking-break red flag). Silence is scoped to Custody; Divorce primaries are firing. (2) a PB-01 budget-lost pattern on 'Westhollow - Divorce' with all gates green on that campaign (budget-lost IS 28% for 2 weeks, converting at target, $5,900/30d, no recent budget/bid change, Divorce primaries firing). Produce the walk card for this account.
evals.expected_output: RED FLAGS block appears first, naming the conversion-silence break on 'Westhollow - Custody'. Exactly one playbook line for PB-01 follows, after the red-flags block, under PLAYBOOKS:. Metrics are reported as separate labelled lines (or short clauses), not as a single comma-chained run of numbers.
evals.trap: Puts the playbook line before or interleaved with the red flag, omits the red-flags block entirely, writes the metrics as one long comma-separated run (e.g. '28%, 2 weeks, $5,900, 22 conv, $291 CPL, no changes' all in a single unlabelled clause), omits the playbook line entirely, or renders the accept-reject decision instead of handing it back.
assertions: [FORMAT] RED FLAGS block appears first and is clearly labelled
[FORMAT] The PB-01 playbook line appears after the RED FLAGS block, not before or mixed into it, under a PLAYBOOKS: header
[FORMAT] Exactly one playbook line appears, and it is identified as PB-01
[FORMAT] Metrics are presented as labelled lines/clauses rather than a single unlabelled comma-chained run of numbers
[OUTPUT DISCIPLINE] The playbook line ends 'accept/reject' and does not characterize the account
evals.notes: Card-format case: red-flags-first ordering plus the ban on comma-chained metric runs, using a genuine red flag paired with a genuine playbook trigger.
evals.retired: Card format and ordering only, no tactic content. Retired 2026-09; not carried into evals_v5.json.

evals.prompt: Account westhollow (fictional), no red flags this check ('RED FLAGS: none'). Four playbook patterns trigger with all gates green: PB-02 on 'Westhollow - Divorce' (rank-lost IS 44%, 2 weeks), PB-15 on 'Westhollow - Custody' (3 keywords all-BELOW_AVERAGE QS components, near-zero impressions, system_serving_status=ELIGIBLE), PB-20 on 'Westhollow - Display Probate' (no ad edit in 7 months, CTR down 19% over 3 months), and PB-29 on 'Westhollow - Brand' (30d CPL up 24% vs prior 30d, conversions within +/-10%, held for 2 consecutive checks). Produce the walk card.
evals.expected_output: The card opens with a RED FLAGS block stating none (literal 'RED FLAGS: none' as the lead). Playbook lines sit under the PLAYBOOKS: group header. Exactly 3 of the 4 triggered playbook lines are carded (evidence tier first, then impact within tier), the 4th is left out of the card with 'surplus journaled: PB-nn' (or 'PLAYBOOKS: 4 triggered, 3 carded' plus that surplus line). No playbook line is phrased as a verdict, and no line is written as a comma-chained metric run.
evals.trap: Cards all 4 lines (exceeds the cap), omits the explicit 'RED FLAGS: none' statement as the lead, omits the PLAYBOOKS: group header, or writes any line as an unlabelled comma-chained metric dump instead of the fixed card-line grammar.
assertions: [FORMAT] The card opens with a RED FLAGS block, stating none (literal 'RED FLAGS: none' as the lead, not a later memo-style 'Red flags this check: None.')
[FORMAT] Playbook lines sit under the literal group header PLAYBOOKS: (or 'PLAYBOOKS: 4 triggered, 3 carded')
[FORMAT] Cards exactly 3 playbook lines, not 4
[FORMAT] The 4th playbook is acknowledged as 'surplus journaled: PB-nn' (or equivalent surplus line), not silently dropped or silently included
[FORMAT] Each carded line follows the grammar 'playbook PB-nn (<scope>): standard move for <pattern> is <move>. accept/reject' rather than a metric-dump sentence
[OUTPUT DISCIPLINE] No line uses banned verdict language ('should', 'needs', 'recommend', 'underperforming', 'the problem is')
evals.notes: Card-format case: the 3-line cap under a 'no red flags' account, plus the explicit 'RED FLAGS: none' requirement and the fixed card-line grammar (vs. a free-form metrics sentence).
evals.retired: Encodes PB-15, retired 2026-09, and a Display-scoped PB-20 leg. Replaced by evals_v5.json case 510.

evals.prompt: Account Apex Law (fictional), campaign 'Westhollow - Custody'. Daily budget was raised from $110 to $198 (+80%) three weeks ago as a deliberate expansion move, confirmed in change history (PF-3). Weekly conversions have risen from 4/week to 7/week over the three weeks since the raise. The 30-day CPL reads $612 against $383 the prior 30-day window (+60%), while 30-day conversions are flat (22 vs 21). Produce the walk card.
evals.expected_output: Reports spend direction, weekly-conversion direction, and 30-day CPL direction as three separate data points. Adds one playbook line: PB-34 hold, naming that the ramp is about three weeks old and the 30-day window has not yet absorbed it, with a review point set around four to six weeks from the raise. States that the 30-day CPL figure is immature relative to the ramp rather than a stable read, and points to the rising weekly-conversion trend as the leading indicator to watch instead.
evals.trap: Fires a PB-29 CPL-creep line off the +60% 30-day figure and proposes decomposing CPC versus CVR, proposes cutting or holding down the budget, treats the 30-day CPL as a stable/current read, or characterizes the campaign as underperforming.
assertions: [PLAYBOOK-LABEL] Emits a labelled PB-34 card line (playbook PB-34 ... accept/reject)
[PLAYBOOK-SUBSTANCE] Holds: names the ramp as about three weeks old, and sets a review point around four to six weeks from the raise, with no immediate action
[DO-NOT-MOVE] Does NOT add a PB-29 CPL-creep line, because the ramp gate (spend moved well outside +/-15%) is not satisfied
[DO-NOT-MOVE] Does NOT propose decomposing CPC versus CVR while the ramp is live (a deferred 'after the ramp window' mention is compliant)
[FALSE-FIRE] Does NOT propose cutting, holding down, or reversing the budget raise based on the 30-day CPL figure
[REASONING] States that the 30-day CPL window is immature / has not yet absorbed the ramp, distinct from calling the campaign's performance bad
[OUTPUT DISCIPLINE] Reports spend direction, weekly-conversion direction, and 30-day CPL direction as separate data points and does not issue a go/no-go or 'underperforming' verdict on the campaign
[COMPLETENESS] Reports the rising weekly-conversion trend (4/week to 7/week) explicitly as the leading indicator alongside the 30-day figure
evals.notes: Pattern validated in practice per playbooks.md PB-34 Evidence field (validated in practice, seven sequential 30-day readings) and PB-29's own Contradiction note, which records that the largest measured PB-29-shaped trigger was itself a ramp in disguise. No client reference; fictional figures only.
unconfirmed: The +/-15% ramp gate separating PB-34 from PB-29 is unconfirmed.

evals.prompt: Account Greenfield Legal (fictional), campaign 'Westhollow - Probate'. search_budget_lost_impression_share = 35%, sustained across the last 2 consecutive complete weeks, rank-lost the smaller component throughout (GAQL 5.1). 30-day CPL = $340 against a confirmed firm target CPL of $400 for this practice area. 30-day conversions = 22. No budget or bid-strategy change in the last 14 days (PF-3 clean). Tracking verified, primaries firing (PF-1 clean). Current daily budget = $85. Produce the walk card.
evals.expected_output: Reports both IS components, 30-day CPL versus target, the conversion count, and the clean pre-flight checks as data. Adds one PB-01 line proposing a single daily-budget raise, sized per the entry (a 20% step on the current $85 budget, since budget-lost sits at a moderate 35% rather than the well-above-50% case that would call for scaling the step to the size of the cap), holding every other setting for 14 days. States the expected result as budget-lost roughly halving rather than clearing, and sets a two-part verification window: impression share / serving re-read at 7 days, conversions re-read at 14 days.
evals.trap: Proposes a step sized to clear budget-lost to near zero in one move, omits stating the step size on the card line, bundles a tCPA or targeting change into the same move, or sets a single flat verification window instead of the 7-day serving / 14-day conversion split.
assertions: [PLAYBOOK] Adds one PB-01 line proposing a single daily-budget raise with the step size named explicitly on the card line
[REASONING] Frames the expected result as budget-lost roughly halving, not clearing, consistent with the entry's measured outcome
[FORMAT] States a two-part verification window: impression share / serving re-read at 7 days, conversions re-read at 14 days
[DO-NOT-MOVE] Does NOT bundle a simultaneous tCPA, keyword, or targeting change into the same move -- budget only, per the entry
[OUTPUT DISCIPLINE] Ends the playbook line with accept/reject and does not issue a go/no-go verdict on the campaign
[COMPLETENESS] Reports the pre-flight checks (PF-1, PF-3) as satisfied before the line is added rather than silently assuming them
evals.notes: Pattern validated in practice per playbooks.md PB-01 Evidence field (validated in practice, 3 outcomes): the step-size framing and the halve-not-clear expectation, plus the 7-day serving / 14-day conversion verification split, both come directly from the entry's measured outcomes. No client reference; fictional figures only.

evals.prompt: Account Apex Law (fictional), campaign 'Westhollow - Elder Abuse'. search_budget_lost_impression_share = 30%, sustained across the last 3 consecutive complete weeks. 30-day conversions = 0. 30-day spend = $4,100, well above 1x the firm's target CPL for this practice area. Sibling campaigns in the account are converting normally and tracking is verified account-wide (PF-1 clean). No recent change (PF-3 clean). Produce the walk card.
evals.expected_output: RED FLAGS block leads the card, naming the 3-consecutive-week zero-conversion streak with material spend ($4,100) as a red flag. Explicitly does NOT add a PB-01 budget-raise line despite the 30% budget-lost figure, citing the PB-01 do-not-move condition (zero conversions in the trailing fortnight). If a playbook line appears at all, it is PB-30, framed as PF-1-first with the campaign-scope branching named, not a spend-side proposal.
evals.trap: Adds a PB-01 raise line because budget-lost is present, treats the zero-conversion streak as ordinary data rather than red-flagging it, or proposes raising the budget as a way to 'test' for conversions or generate signal.
assertions: [DO-NOT-MOVE] Does NOT add a PB-01 budget-raise line despite budget-lost IS = 30%
[CITATION] Names the PB-01 zero-conversions-in-the-trailing-fortnight do-not-move condition (or equivalent: zero conversions in the trailing fortnight)
[RED FLAG] Leads the card with a RED FLAGS block naming the 3-week zero-conversion streak with material spend
[PLAYBOOK] If a playbook line is added, it is PB-30 (or explicitly routes to PB-30's PF-1-first branching), never a spend-side proposal
[FALSE-FIRE] Does NOT propose raising the budget as a way to generate conversion signal or 'test' the campaign
